### Observed differences

- The four activities A36, A37, A42 and A43 each ran in every earlier trace (200 in 200) but in only about half of the later traces (about 100 in 200 each); A27 shows the same drop from every trace to about 100 in 200, and A06 fell from about 63 to about 19 in 200 traces. [OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, OCC001]
- In the earlier window, A25 passed almost always to one of the four group activities (about 98 in 100 of its outgoing transitions, split roughly evenly among them) and almost never straight to A28; in the later window it passes directly to A28 in about 96 in 100, and A28 immediately follows A25 in about 97 in 100 of the observed pairs (earlier, A28 followed A25 five positions later in about 99 in 100). [DIR003, LAG002]
- The group changed sides relative to A28 and A26: earlier, A36/A37/A42/A43 ran before A28 in about 97–99 in 100 of those pairs and before A26 in about 97–99 in 100; in the later window A28 and A26 each precede the group in about 49 in 100 of the traces containing both, with the group absent from the remaining traces. [REL030, REL031, REL032, REL033, REL018, REL019, REL020, REL021]
- A27 and the group, which always executed together earlier (group first, then A27, in about 97–99 in 100), became alternatives: in the later window they co-occur in only about 1 in 200 traces, with A27 alone in about half and the group alone in about half; A26 now routes to A27 in about 49 in 100 of its outgoing transitions and into the group in about 51 in 100, where earlier it went to A27 about 98 in 100. [REL024, REL025, REL026, REL027, DIR004]
- Downstream, the group members now lead to A31 in roughly 18–28 in 100 of their outgoing transitions each, where earlier they led to A28 or among themselves; accordingly, A26 reaches A31 two positions later in about half of the later traces (via A27) and five positions later in the other half (via the group). [DIR005, DIR006, DIR007, DIR008, LAG007, LAG008, LAG009, LAG010, LAG013, LAG016]
- A51 is followed directly by A52 in about 90 in 100 later traces versus about 72 in 100 earlier, consistent with A06 becoming rarer. [LAG018, OCC001]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that, in the later window, the block A36, A37, A42, A43 executes after A26 as an alternative to A27 — in about half of the traces the block runs and A27 is skipped, in the other half A27 runs and the block is skipped — while A25 passes directly to A28 and A31 closes either branch; earlier, every trace executed A25, then the block, then A28, A26, A27 and A31. [DIR003, LAG002, REL018, REL019, REL020, REL021, REL024, REL025, REL026, REL027, DIR004, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006]

The hypothesis is shown directly by relational and lag evidence rather than position shifts alone: A25 reaches A28 within one step, A28 and A26 now precede the block where they previously followed it, A27 and the block are mutually exclusive, and the successor changes at A25, A26 and the block members match this picture. The volume of qualifying items (96 against about 1 expected without a change) rules out chance re-splits as an explanation of the pattern as a whole, and the block's internal behaviour is unchanged — its four activities still run together in mixed order whenever they run. [LAG002, REL024, REL025, REL026, REL027, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, DIR007, DIR008, REL038, REL047]

A competing explanation the evidence cannot rule out is that the block-skipping path already existed as a rare variant before (it appears in 0 of the 200 earlier traces, which is compatible with a prevalence below about 1–2 in 200) and only became frequent, or that the windows sample a shifted mix of two coexisting variants; the samples also cannot establish whether other, unobserved paths changed. [REL024, OCC002]

Other differences: A06 participation fell from about 32 in 100 to about 9.5 in 100 traces and its position became more variable, but its later routing profile rests on only about 19 traces and 17 outgoing transitions, so its new targets are weakly supported; A02's outgoing mix also changed, but with only 5 outgoing transitions observed earlier this is consistent with a rare variant. [OCC001, POS001, DIR002, DIR001]
